$comment: The shared contract for which ledger rows are PARKED. agent-team-template's classify() in scripts/lib/ledger.mjs and agent-cockpit's isParked() in api/state.js make this judgement twice, mirrored by hand because there is no import path between a student's repo and a deployed web app. This is the third such mirror in this pair of repos; the other two are arming-parity.json and knowledge-parity.json, and both of them exist because the two sides drifted. Same bytes in both repos, run by both sides: change one implementation alone and that side fails.
rule: Rule 5, decision-readiness. A row confirmed twice with nobody named to act on its output is parked, not buildable. A fill marker left in the answer counts as no answer. The REASON is not the signal - the format lets an owner park a row without typing one.

cases.label: confirmed twice with somebody named to act on it is not parked

row.hands_off: I read each one and send it myself.

cases.label: confirmed twice with nobody named is parked
parked with no reason typed is still parked
cases.$comment: The case that made the board and the check disagree. The board keyed on the reason having text, which is a narrower rule than check:ledger's, so these rows rendered as live work.

cases.label: parked with a reason typed is parked

row.parked_because: Nobody reads the numbers I send round on Monday.

cases.label: hands_off that is only whitespace is parked
hands_off still carrying a fill marker is no answer, so parked
said once is a note, never parked, whatever hands_off says
cases.$comment: classify() returns note before it ever looks at hands_off. A note is not a decision the owner declined to make - it is something mentioned once, and twice-or-it-is-not-a-pattern is a different rule from decision-readiness.

cases.label: said once with somebody named is still just a note
no confirmed field at all is not parked
an honest negative answer is NOT parked
cases.$comment: check:ledger flags this separately - the answer begins with a negative - but it is a candidate as far as classify() is concerned, because somebody did answer. The board must not quietly reclassify it.

row.hands_off: Nobody - it is my core work.
